metadata.description: Explore 20 of America's most iconic and significant lakes and inland bodies of water.
metadata.author: Journey

journey.name: Great American Lakes
journey.description: Explore 20 remarkable American lakes and inland bodies of water, from all five Great Lakes to alpine, volcanic, desert, prairie, and coastal waters across the country.

items.name: Lake Superior
items.description: The largest of the Great Lakes by surface area, Lake Superior is renowned for its immense scale, rugged cliffs, clear cold water, islands, and dramatic North Shore scenery.

items.name: Lake Michigan
items.description: The only Great Lake located entirely within the United States, Lake Michigan is bordered by sweeping dunes, major cities, beaches, lighthouses, and distinctive freshwater coastlines.

items.name: Lake Huron
items.description: Known for its enormous shoreline, clear blue water, countless islands, and Georgian Bay, Lake Huron forms a vast freshwater landscape along Michigan and Ontario.

items.name: Lake Erie
items.description: The shallowest of the Great Lakes, Lake Erie combines broad freshwater horizons, island chains, productive fisheries, beaches, and major waterfront cities.

items.name: Lake Ontario
items.description: The easternmost Great Lake, Lake Ontario connects the Great Lakes system to the St. Lawrence River and is framed by major cities, islands, bluffs, and fertile shoreline.

items.name: Lake Tahoe
items.description: A spectacular alpine lake on the California-Nevada border, Lake Tahoe is celebrated for exceptionally clear blue water, granite mountains, beaches, and year-round recreation.

items.name: Great Salt Lake
items.description: A vast terminal salt lake in northern Utah, the Great Salt Lake is famous for broad horizons, distinctive islands, mineral-rich water, wetlands, and enormous migratory bird populations.

items.name: Lake Okeechobee
items.description: Florida's largest freshwater lake is a defining feature of South Florida, supporting wetlands, fisheries, wildlife, recreation, and the greater Everglades watershed.

items.name: Lake Champlain
items.description: Stretching between New York and Vermont, Lake Champlain combines Adirondack and Green Mountain scenery with islands, historic communities, boating, and a rich maritime heritage.

items.name: Lake of the Woods
items.description: A sprawling international lake shared by Minnesota and Canada, Lake of the Woods is a maze of islands, bays, forests, fishing waters, and remote northern shorelines.

items.name: Crater Lake
items.description: Formed within the collapsed caldera of Mount Mazama, Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States and is renowned for intensely blue water and steep volcanic walls.

items.name: Lake Powell
items.description: This immense Colorado River reservoir winds through red-rock canyon country in Utah and Arizona, creating a striking landscape of sandstone cliffs, side canyons, and blue water.

items.name: Lake Mead
items.description: Created by Hoover Dam on the Colorado River, Lake Mead spreads through desert canyons in Nevada and Arizona and remains one of America's most recognizable reservoirs.

items.name: Lake Pontchartrain
items.description: A broad brackish estuary bordering New Orleans, Lake Pontchartrain connects southeastern Louisiana's wetlands and waterways with the Gulf of Mexico.

items.name: Lake Sakakawea
items.description: One of the largest reservoirs in the United States, Lake Sakakawea stretches across the Missouri River landscape of western North Dakota with long bays, bluffs, and open prairie.

items.name: Lake Pend Oreille
items.description: Surrounded by forested mountains in northern Idaho, Lake Pend Oreille is one of the deepest lakes in the United States and is known for clear water and dramatic scenery.

items.name: Flathead Lake
items.description: A broad natural freshwater lake in northwestern Montana, Flathead Lake is framed by mountain ranges, orchards, islands, and exceptionally scenic shoreline.

items.name: Yellowstone Lake
items.description: Set high on the Yellowstone Plateau, Yellowstone Lake is North America's largest high-elevation lake of its size and is surrounded by volcanic, geothermal, and wilderness landscapes.

items.name: Lake George
items.description: A long, narrow Adirondack lake in eastern New York, Lake George is known for forested mountains, islands, historic sites, clear water, and a centuries-old resort tradition.

items.name: Lake Winnipesaukee
items.description: New Hampshire's largest lake is a classic New England destination of wooded islands, mountain views, historic towns, boating, beaches, and lakeside recreation.
